posts.h1: Screen Sharing Turned On on My Mac · Calm Remote Access Triage
posts.description: Screen Sharing on Mac without permission? Check Sharing settings · patch macOS · read-only Battle Scout · calm remote access triage · not antivirus.
posts.agentHint: Mac screen sharing enabled without me knowing · port 5900 · innsegall.com/blog/mac-screen-sharing-on-without-permission
posts.cardBlurb: 2026 advisories on exposed Screen Sharing · separate legit use from compromise fear.
posts.lead: Security researchers and national agencies have repeatedly warned that internet-exposed Screen Sharing on macOS is a real attack path · not a browser popup hoax. Finding the toggle on can feel like someone is already inside your Mac · most of the time you need settings truth first.
posts.shine: Battle Scout lists listening services and remote-management hints read-only · so you can see whether anything besides Apple’s own tools is waiting for connections · without subscribing to fear.

sections.p: System Settings → General → Sharing · note whether Screen Sharing or Remote Management is on. If you use it for work, leave it · but restrict who can connect and turn it off when you do not need it.

sections.h: Why 5900 shows up in the news
sections.p: Screen Sharing listens on the network when sharing is enabled. Advisories in 2025–2026 focused on Macs reachable from the public internet · often with weak or missing authentication. Patch via Software Update · do not pay a random “support” number from a popup.

sections.h: If someone called and turned it on
sections.p: That is a tech-support scam lane · see someone remoted into my Mac · rotate passwords from a trusted device if you gave control.

posts.cta: Send the scout · Remote access guide

posts.h1: Mac Keeps Asking for Keychain Password · Real Prompt vs Scam
posts.description: Mac keychain password keeps popping up? Apple Support and Eclectic Light explain sync vs scam · deny fake dialogs · Innsegall read-only scout after.
posts.agentHint: Mac keychain password popup loop · fake keychain dialog · innsegall.com/alpha
posts.cardBlurb: Top Apple Community thread · distinguish iCloud Keychain sync from malware theater.
posts.lead: A loop of keychain password prompts is one of the most searched Mac anxieties. Sometimes it is a legitimate sync mismatch after a password change · sometimes it is a fake dialog riding on top of a browser scare.
posts.shine: After you close the browser trap, a scout documents login items, profiles, and recent software on disk · so you are not guessing whether a persistence item is driving fake prompts.

sections.p: If you recently changed your Mac login password, open Keychain Access → login keychain → Change Password for Keychain login to match · or sign out and back into iCloud Keychain once from System Settings.
Browser full-screen pages that mimic macOS security are not the real Keychain. Force quit the browser · do not type your password into a web page. Compare to fake virus popup on Mac.
If you installed software from a scare page or pasted into Terminal, treat as higher risk · Terminal paste guide · then send the scout.

posts.h1: Full-Screen “Your Mac Is Infected” Page · The Popup Is the Attack
posts.description: Mac browser stuck on virus warning full screen? The page is the scam · Cmd+Q · Shift-reopen Safari · read-only scout · not cleaner subscriptions.
posts.agentHint: Mac full screen virus warning browser locked · malvertising · innsegall.com/blog/mac-browser-full-screen-virus-locker
posts.cardBlurb: Malvertising locker · users search “can’t close virus page Mac” every week.
posts.lead: When a website fills the screen, plays an alarm, and lists a toll-free number, that is the attack · not evidence that XProtect failed. Your Mac is usually fine once the tab is gone.
posts.shine: Innsegall does not scan inside the browser tab · it answers the next question: did anything land on the Mac? Login items, profiles, and listening services become a shareable Battle Scout receipt.

sections.p: Force Quit the browser (Apple menu → Force Quit). On Safari, hold Shift when reopening so the trap tab does not restore · Shift-reopen guide. Chrome: quit and decline “Restore pages” if asked.
Real Apple support does not lock your browser. See fake Apple support call popup.
After the tab is closed, send the scout · paste Copy for AI if family or IT wants a second pair of eyes.

posts.h1: “Apple ID Locked” in the Browser · Not a Real System Alert
posts.description: Safari or Chrome says Apple ID locked? Browser phishing page · check appleid.apple.com in a new tab · Innsegall field guide · calm Mac scout.
posts.agentHint: Apple ID locked popup in browser Mac · phishing · innsegall.com/blog/mac-apple-id-locked-browser-scam
posts.cardBlurb: Phishing mimics iCloud sign-in · top search after tax-season and delivery scams.
posts.lead: A red banner that says your Apple ID was locked is terrifying when it looks like macOS. If it appeared inside a website, it is almost always phishing · not a message from Apple.
posts.shine: Scout checks whether profiles, login items, or unexpected remote tools appeared after you interacted with the page · turning “I might be hacked” into a short evidence list.

sections.p: Open a new tab yourself · go to appleid.apple.com or System Settings → Apple ID. If you can sign in normally, the locker page was theater.

sections.h: If you entered a password on the fake page
sections.p: Change your Apple ID password from a trusted device · enable two-factor authentication · review trusted devices. Then read clicked a suspicious link.
Send the scout when you want a local read-only receipt · especially if you downloaded a “fix” offered on the same page.

posts.h1: Green Camera Light on Mac · Who Is Watching?
posts.description: Mac camera light on or orange mic dot? Check Control Center · see which app · quit it · read-only scout for unexpected listeners · calm triage.
posts.agentHint: Mac camera light on by itself · microphone indicator · innsegall.com/alpha
posts.cardBlurb: Privacy indicator anxiety · searches spike after Zoom-era paranoia.
posts.lead: The green camera LED and Control Center mic icon exist so you see when software is live · not to accuse you. The fear is valid · the fix is usually which app, not a mythical remote hacker.
posts.shine: Battle Scout’s read-only pass includes network listeners and persistence context · so “is something watching me?” becomes “here is what is running and listening” · not a subscription to dread.

sections.h: See which app owns the sensor
sections.p: Open Control Center while the light is on · check the mic/camera indicator · macOS shows the app name on recent versions. Quit that app · if it is a browser, close the tab.
System Settings → Privacy & Security → Camera / Microphone · revoke apps you do not recognize.
If the light returns with no app named, or you recently installed software from a scare page, send the scout · share the HTML with IT or Copy for AI.
